claim: Format B is selected with a brief main message, expandable evidence and a one-dimension clarification. It will be tested in the v2.2 release candidate.
evidence: Eighty-six percent of participants correctly identified why the system abstained with format B, compared with 58 percent for format A.
Average trust was 4.3 out of 5 with format B and 3.5 with A. However, B messages took longer to read.
Eighty-one percent of clarifications were considered useful. The poorest cases added two details at once, such as date and unit.
Participants detected the error more readily when evidence was shown. That reduces false confidence, although it does not eliminate false abstention.
